title: An evaluation of the training determinants of marathon performance: A meta-analysis with meta-regression
authors: Doherty C, Keogh A, Davenport J, Lawlor A, Smyth B, Caulfield B
journal: Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport
population: Elite and recreational marathon runners (25% female) in 85 observational and interventional studies (137 cohorts)
findings: 85 studies with 137 cohorts of runners (25% female) were included in the meta-regression.

Covariates: average weekly running distance, number of weekly runs, maximum distance in a single week, number of runs of 32 km or more in the pre-marathon block, average training pace, longest-run distance and hours of running per week.

Separate univariate random-effects meta-regressions found a negative association between each behaviour and marathon time (R2 0.38-0.81, p<0.001): increases in a training parameter coincided with faster finish times.
Meta-analysis estimated the marathon non-finisher rate at 7.27% (95% CI 6.09% to 8.65%).
limitations: Between-cohort (ecological) associations from observational data; univariate models, so the covariates are collinear and not separated; no per-athlete causality; heterogeneous measurement; faster cohorts differ in talent and history. The abstract gives only direction and an R2 range, no coefficients. Monotone associations say nothing about diminishing returns or injury cost.
implications: Treat weekly distance, runs per week, longest run, count of 32 km+ runs and training pace as monotone predictors of marathon time and scale targets to the goal time band instead of one template.
Do not hard-code numeric volume bands from this abstract; calibrate from full-text coefficients or from larger datasets (Muniz-Pumares 2025, Fokkema 2020).
Use about 7% as the baseline population non-finish rate when describing risk.

verification.notes: Crossref (issued 2020-02), title, journal and first author match; abstract re-fetched from Europe PMC and all numbers checked. Level lowered from A to B because the meta-regression is univariate and ecological. Full text not read.
